shortlist.name: China Investment Corporation — CIC International
shortlist.invests: Yes — large offshore external-manager book for public equities, hedge funds and multi-asset
shortlist.angle: An existing relationship and the single best door in China: unlike most mainland institutions, CIC International genuinely runs USD external mandates and specifically wants differentiated China/Asia alpha from an on-the-ground manager.
shortlist.access: Warm relationship, routed to CIC International's public-equities / hedge-fund manager-selection desk.
shortlist.watchout: Large-ticket bias and a formal RFP cadence; show institutional operations and capacity to absorb size.

shortlist.name: Silk Road Fund
shortlist.invests: Selective — a state investment vehicle (SAFE/CIC/Exim/CDB-funded); the live dialogue is the point
shortlist.angle: A live conversation, which makes it very relevant regardless of its usual mandate. Silk Road is USD-capitalised and state-backed; the task is to shape a mandate that fits its cross-border / strategic remit and keep the relationship advancing.
shortlist.access: Continue the existing dialogue; align on a structure (bespoke mandate / China-Asia strategy / co-investment angle) that fits its remit.
shortlist.watchout: Historically a Belt-and-Road direct-finance investor, so a plain listed-equities mandate may need reframing; keep the relationship warm and let them define the vehicle.

shortlist.name: National Council for Social Security Fund (NSSF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — outsources ~2/3 of assets; has awarded offshore USD equity/FI mandates to global managers since 2006
shortlist.angle: China's sovereign pension reserve is one of the very few mainland allocators that awards genuine offshore USD mandates to external managers, and it values long-horizon, governance-strong partners for its China/Asia sleeves.
shortlist.access: NSSF's overseas-investment department; mandate cycles are periodic and highly selective.
shortlist.watchout: Prizes stability and track record; not a fast or a first-fund decision.

shortlist.name: China Taiping Insurance / Taiping Financial Holdings
shortlist.invests: Selective — its Hong Kong-based Taiping Financial Holdings deploys insurance assets offshore, including via external managers
shortlist.angle: The most offshore-native large Chinese insurer: being Hong Kong-headquartered, it can allocate USD offshore without the QDII constraints that sideline mainland peers, and it values local managers who understand the region.
shortlist.access: Taiping Financial Holdings' Hong Kong asset-management team.
shortlist.watchout: Still largely in-house; external mandates are selective and insurance-liability aware.

shortlist.name: HKMA — Exchange Fund
shortlist.invests: Yes — the Investment Portfolio and the Long-Term Growth Portfolio both hire external managers
shortlist.angle: A live conversation and a genuine fund-LP: the HKMA runs external-manager mandates through both its Investment Portfolio (public markets) and its Long-Term Growth Portfolio, and being the home regulator's fund makes local standing a real advantage.
shortlist.access: Continue the existing dialogue with the HKMA's external-managers / Exchange Fund investment teams.
shortlist.watchout: Institutional scale and process; the public-markets external book is more selective than the private-markets LTGP.

shortlist.name: The Hong Kong Jockey Club (Charities Trust)
shortlist.invests: Yes — ~25% in alternatives incl. hedge funds, via external managers
shortlist.angle: A large, sophisticated local endowment-style pool that already runs an external hedge-fund and alternatives programme in USD, reachable on home turf — an ideal early institutional reference LP.
shortlist.access: HKJC investment office directly; local relationships shorten the path.
shortlist.watchout: Institutional-grade diligence despite being local.

shortlist.name: VMS Group
shortlist.invests: Yes — purpose-built to seed and accelerate managers, incl. long/short equity
shortlist.angle: A Cheng-family-backed HK seeder explicitly building a long/short equity platform — it exists to provide anchor capital and infrastructure to managers like us, on home turf and in USD.
shortlist.access: VMS's seeding / acceleration team directly.
shortlist.watchout: Primarily relevant if the vehicle is long/short; seed economics (revenue share / equity) attach.

shortlist.name: Sun Hung Kai & Co. Limited (SHK Capital Partners)
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates to external hedge funds via its multi-manager platform and can anchor with principal capital
shortlist.angle: A listed HK investment firm that both allocates to external managers and deploys balance-sheet capital to anchor them — a rare local source of day-one USD anchor money. (Distinct from Sun Hung Kai Properties.)
shortlist.access: SHK Capital Partners / the multi-manager team, locally.
shortlist.watchout: Meaningful but not sovereign-scale cheques; align on terms.

shortlist.name: Nan Fung Group / NF Trinity
shortlist.invests: Yes — documented external-manager programme that backs promising newer managers
shortlist.angle: A major HK family office with a real, documented programme of backing external and emerging managers in public markets — a warm, local, USD-capable early backer.
shortlist.access: NF Trinity's investment team; local family-office network.
shortlist.watchout: Discreet and relationship-led; sizing varies.

shortlist.name: Carret Private Capital
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates client capital to external funds
shortlist.angle: A HK multi-family office with a value-investing orientation that allocates USD to external managers — a natural fit for a fundamental, research-driven process.
shortlist.access: Carret's manager-selection team, locally.
shortlist.watchout: FO-scale cheques; needs a clear fit with their house style.

shortlist.name: Raffles Family Office
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates client capital to external funds across Asia
shortlist.angle: One of Asia's larger multi-family offices (HK/Singapore), actively deploying client USD capital into external funds — a scalable channel to Asian family-office money.
shortlist.access: RFO's investment office; HK and Singapore desks.
shortlist.watchout: Gatekept by their fund-selection process; sizing per underlying family.

shortlist.name: AIA Group
shortlist.invests: Selective — uses external managers to complement in-house across pan-Asia
shortlist.angle: A HK-headquartered pan-Asian insurer that selectively hires external managers and understands the region; a differentiated Asia strategy can complement its in-house books.
shortlist.access: AIA Investment Management; frame around diversifying, liability-aware Asia exposure.
shortlist.watchout: Largely in-house; external mandates are selective.

shortlist.name: GIC
shortlist.invests: Yes — very large external-manager programme incl. Asian/EM equities and hedge funds
shortlist.angle: A core, permanent user of external managers that specifically hunts differentiated Asia and emerging-market alpha — a credible research-driven Asia manager is squarely in its wheelhouse.
shortlist.access: GIC's External Managers Department (public equities / hedge funds); a warm intro materially helps.
shortlist.watchout: Rigorous multi-year diligence and a capacity preference; rarely a first-fund seed.

shortlist.name: Temasek — Seviora (Fullerton / SeaTown)
shortlist.invests: Selective — Temasek is direct-heavy, but its Seviora asset managers (Fullerton, SeaTown) can allocate / co-invest
shortlist.angle: Temasek proper is direct-heavy, but its Seviora managers (Fullerton, SeaTown) are the realistic route for external or co-investment capital tied to Asia.
shortlist.access: Seviora / SeaTown, rather than Temasek's direct-investing teams.
shortlist.watchout: Temasek itself rarely acts as a fund LP; keep expectations on the asset-management arm.

shortlist.name: Bank of Singapore (OCBC)
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates discretionary client capital and places funds onto its Asian wealth platform
shortlist.angle: A pure Asian private bank that aggregates HNW / family-office USD capital and can channel it into a fund; its clients actively want Asia strategies.
shortlist.access: Bank of Singapore's funds / discretionary-portfolio and manager-selection teams.
shortlist.watchout: Platform onboarding and suitability requirements for client money.

shortlist.name: Public Officials Benefit Association (POBA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — very active overseas allocator, known to back specialist and newer managers
shortlist.angle: POBA is nimble, overseas-hungry and unusually willing to back specialist / emerging managers — the best-fit Korean allocator for a manager still building scale.
shortlist.access: POBA's CIO office; typically via placement agents / consultants and Seoul roadshows.
shortlist.watchout: Cheques sized to a mid-size fund; competitive process.

shortlist.name: National Pension Service (NPS)
shortlist.invests: Yes — large overseas external-manager and hedge-fund programmes via RFP
shortlist.angle: The world's third-largest pension is an aggressive overseas allocator that routinely hires external managers for global/Asia equities and hedge funds via formal RFPs.
shortlist.access: NPS overseas-investment / hedge-fund RFPs, via consultants and Seoul roadshows.
shortlist.watchout: Track-record and AUM thresholds; a structured, competitive RFP.

shortlist.name: Korea Investment Corporation (KIC)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers across equities and hedge funds
shortlist.angle: Korea's sovereign fund is a committed external-manager user with a global remit and appetite for differentiated overseas alpha.
shortlist.access: KIC's external-management team; Seoul-based process.
shortlist.watchout: Institutional thresholds; competitive selection.

shortlist.name: Korea Teachers' Pension / Korea Post
shortlist.invests: Yes — regular overseas external mandates via RFP
shortlist.angle: Second-tier Korean asset owners that consistently award overseas USD mandates to external managers and are more approachable than NPS for a mid-size manager.
shortlist.access: Their overseas-investment teams via RFP / placement agents.
shortlist.watchout: Smaller tickets; RFP-driven and consultant-influenced.

shortlist.name: Pension Fund Association (PFA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — sophisticated user of external managers, incl. hedge funds and overseas equities
shortlist.angle: Japan's most sophisticated corporate-pension aggregator, genuinely open to overseas and alternative managers, and a reference name that pulls other Japanese pensions along.
shortlist.access: Usually intermediated by Japanese trust-bank gatekeepers / consultants.
shortlist.watchout: Slow, consensus-driven; near-always gatekeeper-gated.

shortlist.name: Japanese trust-bank gatekeepers (Sumitomo Mitsui Trust / MUFG Trust / Nomura EMP)
shortlist.invests: They select and package external managers for many Japanese pension clients; Japan's Emerging Managers Programme explicitly welcomes foreign/newer managers
shortlist.angle: In Japan the gatekeeper is the market: one approval by a trust-bank platform or the government-backed Emerging Managers Programme unlocks capital from many underlying pensions at once — an efficient route for a foreign manager.
shortlist.access: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust / MUFG Trust manager-research desks; Nomura / SMBC EMP mandates.
shortlist.watchout: Long onboarding and Japanese-language / local-presence expectations.

shortlist.name: Japan Post Bank
shortlist.invests: Yes — large and growing alternatives book placed with external managers
shortlist.angle: A vast balance sheet running a fast-growing alternatives programme through external managers and diversifying overseas — real USD capital if accessed via the right gatekeeper.
shortlist.access: Via trust-bank gatekeepers / its alternatives team.
shortlist.watchout: Scale and process bias toward larger, established managers.

shortlist.name: Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers for global equities; expanding its manager pool
shortlist.angle: The world's largest pension uses external managers for global equities and has been widening its roster — the ultimate anchor, but a multi-year aspiration for our size.
shortlist.access: GPIF manager structure, via gatekeepers; extremely high bar.
shortlist.watchout: Scale and track-record thresholds make it aspirational, not first-wave.

shortlist.name: Taiwan Bureau of Labor Funds (BLF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — regularly awards multi-year foreign (USD) equity mandates to external managers via public tender
shortlist.angle: One of Asia's most reliable sources of external mandates: BLF runs recurring public tenders for global and regional equity mandates in USD, awarded to external managers — a structured, repeatable entry point.
shortlist.access: BLF's public tender process, typically supported by global consultants.
shortlist.watchout: Tender criteria favour firm-level track record and AUM; fee-competitive.

shortlist.name: Employees Provident Fund (EPF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external global mandates (incl. USD and Shariah) to external managers
shortlist.angle: A very large provident fund that outsources global equity mandates to external managers in USD and is diversifying beyond Malaysia.
shortlist.access: EPF's external-mandate / global-investment teams.
shortlist.watchout: Bureaucratic; some mandates carry Shariah or ESG constraints.

shortlist.name: Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (KWAP)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers for international equities
shortlist.angle: Malaysia's civil-service pension allocates internationally through external managers and is expanding overseas exposure — a mid-size USD mandate route.
shortlist.access: KWAP's international / external-manager desk.
shortlist.watchout: Smaller tickets; competitive and consultant-influenced.

shortlist.name: Government Pension Fund (Thailand)
shortlist.invests: Yes — awards global equity mandates to external managers
shortlist.angle: Thailand's main public pension outsources part of its global book to external managers in USD and has been steadily raising its foreign allocation.
shortlist.access: GPF's investment team; mandate awards often consultant-supported.
shortlist.watchout: Smaller tickets; governance-driven, periodic mandate cycles.

shortlist.name: Future Fund
shortlist.invests: Yes — largely outsourced to external managers, incl. hedge funds and Asia
shortlist.angle: Australia's sovereign fund runs a near-fully-outsourced model and actively backs specialist external managers, with real hedge-fund and Asia appetite.
shortlist.access: Future Fund's external-manager teams (Melbourne).
shortlist.watchout: High bar; prefers demonstrable edge and capacity.

shortlist.name: Hostplus
shortlist.invests: Yes — outsourced multi-manager, notably willing to back specialist / emerging managers (JANA-advised)
shortlist.angle: Among the Australian supers, Hostplus is the standout for backing specialist and emerging managers through an outsourced model — a rare institutional early-backer.
shortlist.access: Via its asset consultant JANA, and the Hostplus investment team.
shortlist.watchout: Consultant-gated (a JANA rating is effectively the gate); AUD home bias.

shortlist.name: New Zealand Superannuation Fund
shortlist.invests: Yes — active external-manager programme, contrarian / opportunistic
shortlist.angle: A sophisticated, approachable sovereign fund with an active external-manager programme and a genuinely thesis-driven culture that engages differentiated managers.
shortlist.access: Guardians of NZ Super's external-investments team (Auckland).
shortlist.watchout: Small team, high selectivity; wants a clear, articulable edge.

shortlist.name: Julius Baer (Asia)
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates client / advisory capital to external funds; strong HK / Singapore presence
shortlist.angle: A pure-play private bank with a large Asian booking centre that can aggregate HNW / family-office USD capital into a fund, and whose Asian clients actively want Asia strategies.
shortlist.access: Julius Baer's fund-research and Asia investment teams (Hong Kong / Singapore).
shortlist.watchout: Platform onboarding and suitability requirements; client-money DD.

shortlist.name: UBS Global Wealth Management (Asia)
shortlist.invests: Yes — aggregates HNW / family-office capital onto its fund platform; the largest Asian wealth franchise
shortlist.angle: The world's largest wealth manager, with the biggest Asian booking centre; it can aggregate substantial HNW and family-office USD capital into a single fund, and its Asian clients actively seek Asia strategies.
shortlist.access: UBS GWM's hedge-fund / alternatives fund-selection and Asia teams (Hong Kong / Singapore).
shortlist.watchout: Rigorous platform onboarding; suitability and capacity requirements for client money.

shortlist.name: Landmark Family Office
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates Asian family-office client capital to external funds
shortlist.angle: A regional multi-family office channel to Asian family-office USD capital, reachable locally and open to differentiated managers.
shortlist.access: Landmark's investment / manager-selection team.
shortlist.watchout: FO-scale tickets; gated by their fund-selection view.
